statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Company Name Reservation and Registration Portal (administered by the Ministry of Business, Innovation & Employment, Companies Register, NZBN)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin/Roman characters; Māori names are permitted with correct macron usage where applicable. Non-Latin scripts (including Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic, or Devanagari) are not accepted for the registered company name; only a phonetic or direct Latin-script romanization may be submitted. The name must not be identical or nearly identical to a name already reserved or registered, must not be offensive or contrary to public policy, and must end with 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation unless an exemption applies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Companies Office rejects a proposed name, the applicant must first file a 'Notice of Request for Name Reconsideration' via the Companies Office online portal within 20 working days of the rejection notice, specifying the grounds for reconsideration under sections 20 and 21 of the Companies Act 1993. The Registrar shall provide written reasons; if the reconsideration remains refused, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand by way of judicial review within 20 working days after the final written decision. The applicant may simultaneously reserve an alternative name without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the registered office requirement under section 190 of the Companies Act 1993, provided the registered office address is a physical street address capable of receiving service of process and mail; a PO Box number or electronic address is insufficient. Virtual-office providers that accept legal process and maintain secure document custody are compliant. However, for a virtual CFO consultancy classified as low AMLCFT risk, the registered office must correspond to an actual physical location of the resident agent or an identifiable reception point, and the company must be able to produce original books and records on demand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approx. 10–15% annual probability for a newly incorporated non-trading virtual CFO services entity; may rise above 25% if the company obtains a financial service provider license or holds metro-class trust or custody assets)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 11-16, 19-21 and 151-155 (incorporation, certificate, name, directors' residence and consent); Financial Reporting Act 2013 (statutory financial reporting and audit exemption thresholds); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, Part 6 (Financial Advice Provider licensing); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT reporting entity obligations); Income Tax Act 2007 (IRD registration and taxation of overseas-sourced income).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (an operational business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, MBIE), administratively housed at the Companies Register online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Application (the online prescribed form lodged through the New Zealand Companies Register e-filing channel, with the company constitution and written consents annexed where applicable).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a private company limited by shares under the Companies Act 1993. At least one share must be issued; shares carry no par value and may be issued fully paid, partly paid, or for non-cash consideration determined by directors. No escrow account or bank capital deposit is required for a non-deposit-taking professional services company. The incorporation application must specify the share classes (if any), the maximum number of shares issuable, and each shareholder's initial share subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Constitution of the Company, as follows: (1) SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: THAT the Company shall issue, immediately effective upon registration, a total of one thousand (1,000) ordinary shares without par value at a subscription price of NZD 1.00 per share to each founding subscriber as set out in the incorporation application, such shares to be fully paid and duly credited in the Company's share register, and THAT the directors be and are hereby authorised to accept any further subscriptions of ordinary shares within the authorised maximum of the Company. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: THAT the registered office of the Company shall be and is hereby fixed at the address of the Company's New Zealand registered office as notified in the incorporation application (being a physical address in New Zealand, not a post-office box), and THAT the board approves the written consent of the registered office holder and the lodgment of all required notices with the Registrar of Companies. (3) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: THAT the following persons be and are hereby appointed to the offices indicated, each to act from the date of incorporation until removed or resignation pursuant to the constitution: [Name] as Chief Financial Officer and Managing Director; [Name] as Company Secretary; and [Name] as AML/CFT Compliance Officer (where applicable). (4) DELEGATION AND BANKING: THAT the Managing Director be and is hereby authorised, jointly with any other director, to open, operate and close corporate bank and electronic money accounts with licensed banks and approved payment processors (including Stripe Billing and Wise), and to execute all account documentation on behalf of the Company. (5) ADOPTION OF GOVERNANCE DOCUMENTS: THAT the proposed constitution, the internal governance structure, and the authorised signatory schedule be and are hereby adopted, and the directors are authorised to file all statutory returns and to procure the issuance of the certificate of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Screening and Statutory Availability Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register name search facility, business.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a formal name availability search on the Companies Register against existing registered company names, reserved names, and prohibited or restricted words pursuant to section 20 of the Companies Act 1993. If the proposed name is identical to an existing name or is otherwise misleading, offensive, or connotes government affiliation, select a variant or obtain a written consent from the affected entity. After the internal name check is passed, the name is submitted for final screening at the time of incorporation lodgment - no standalone reservation fee applies in New Zealand.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternative name variants
Completed name availability search results
Written consent of any person whose approval is required for restricted words
Authorisation from the founding shareholders for the name selection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries or refuses the name, promptly file a written response to the Companies Office within 10 working days by counter-proposing a new name or providing a letter of consent from the name owner; a refused name can be re-submitted in amended form as part of a fresh incorporation application without additional regulatory penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment of the Company Incorporation Application and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies - New Zealand Companies Office (online Companies Register e-filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the incorporation application by populating the prescribed online form fields: company name, registered office physical address (subject at all times to a landowner's authority), constitution (adopted by all subscribers as summarised in the board resolution), shareholder particulars, director particulars (at least one natural person resident in New Zealand), and share structure. Each founding director must deliver a signed written consent to act as a director under section 152 of the Companies Act 1993. Pay the prescribed statutory incorporation fee online by credit card or approved payment interface; upon successful validation, the Registrar will automatically validate the application against the Companies Act requirements and issue the entity in the Companies Register.
required_dossiers: Completed Companies Register incorporation application form
Constitution of the company (if adopted)
Written consents to act as director of each proposed director
Shareholder consent and share subscription agreement
Proof of registry fee payment
Registered office holder's consent and landowner's authority (if the registered office is not the company's own premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is placed in query status by the Companies Office, the incorporator must access the Companies Register portal within 10 working days, upload responsive documentation (corrected constitution, valid director consents, or accurate registered office address), and resubmit. Where the Registrar declines registration, the applicant may resubmit a corrected application without prejudice or apply to the High Court for review of the Registrar's decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (automatic NZBN allocation through the Government Business Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon statutory registration under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation (electronic format) and automatically allocates a 13-digit New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) uniquely identifying the company on the national business register. The company should download and archive the certificate and NZBN record, populate the NZBN registry entry with the ISIC 6920 / NAICS 541219 activity descriptors (fractional CFO advisory and multicurrency ledger bookkeeping), and publish the registered office particulars before commencing trading activities.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the electronic Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation notice
Company constitution and board resolution package
Share register and director consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or NZBN is not issued within the service standard, write to the Companies Office with the electronic transaction number and request re-issuance; any discrepancy in the registered office, director, or share data is corrected through a compliant 'Change Particulars' filing, and the certificate is re-issued upon payment of the prescribed alteration fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration (IRD, GST, PAYE and Digital Services Tax Filings)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake, IRD) - New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company through the IRD's myIR portal using the NZBN to obtain a non-resident/standard IRD number for income tax. Apply for GST registration immediately (voluntary registration is permitted) where the virtual CFO services are expected to exceed the NZD 60,000 annual taxable supply threshold or where foreign supplier registration is advantageous; file GST returns on a standard or special basis with 15% GST applying to NZ-resident digital services. Register as an employer for PAYE/ESCT if staff will be recruited in New Zealand. Confirm the tax treatment of the International Company: a company incorporated in NZ is ordinarily NZ tax resident, and the directors must therefore assess any foreign-sourced income assertions against section YD 2 of the Income Tax Act 2007.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN
IRD company income tax registration questionnaire
Identities and addresses of directors, substantial shareholders and beneficial owners
Bank account details for IRD refund/credit transactions
Financial reporting framework selection statement (NZ IFRS or external reporting framework)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD queries the registration or the tax residence / permanent establishment position, submit a written technical position paper with supporting authority from the Income Tax Act 2007 and double-tax treaties, furnish the required statutory declarations, and file an administrative review request with the IRD disputes unit; the company may likewise apply for a binding tax ruling on cross-border withholding rates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Advice Provider Licensing and AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and Department of Internal Affairs (DIA, AML/CFT Group)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess whether the virtual CFO advisory mandates constitute regulated financial advice on debt, equity, or derivative products under Part 6 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. If so, apply to the FMA for a private or full Financial Advice Provider (FAP) licence: the application must describe the advice services, disclose the responsible persons, adopt a risk and compliance programme, provide a reasonable steps business continuity policy, subscribe to an approved external dispute resolution scheme (e.g., Financial Services Complaints Limited), and prepare disclosure statements for retail clients. In parallel, file the AML/CFT compliance programme and supervisor registration with the DIA because the company's accounting / ledger / CFO bookkeeping activities involve providing financial-related services and may be subject to the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, including customer due diligence, record-keeping, suspicious transaction reporting, and the appointment of a compliance officer.
required_dossiers: FMA FAP licence application (Part 6 FMCA)
AML/CFT compliance programme and business risk assessment
Financial crime, terrorism financing and proliferation financing risk assessment
Certified evidence of professional indemnity insurance
Disclosure statements and complaints handling manual
Chartered Accountants ANZ / CPA / equivalent professional certification evidence
Register of responsible persons for financial advice purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA/DIA queries the application, respond with supplementary policies and auditable evidence within the statutory response window (generally 10 working days); if the FAP licence is declined, the company may restructure the business as an agent of an existing licensed FAP or appeal the decision to the High Court under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 at the expiry of the reconsideration process. For AML/CFT registration, any adverse finding may be cured by submitting the revised compliance programme and board-approved remedial plan to the DIA and, failing that, by seeking judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Banking and International Payment Rails Onboarding (Stripe Billing and Wise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand banks and licensed payment service providers; regulated under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a designated New Zealand corporate current account (multi-currency) with a licensed bank or non-bank deposit taker presenting the certificate of incorporation, NZBN, constitution, and director identities. Simultaneously initiate merchant onboarding with Stripe Billing (for subscription-based fractional CFO fees) and Wise (for multicurrency ledger settlement), each requiring KYC/AML verification of the company, beneficial owners, and signatories. Configure the payment rail routing protocol, including mandatory customer identifier fields, to reflect the accountant exemption thresholds under the AML/CFT Act, and ensure all incoming client funds for the virtual CFO service are segregated from operating capital to comply with trust-account obligations (if applicable).
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN
Company constitution and current shareholders/directors register
Photographic identification of signatories and beneficial owners (passport / national identity certificate)
AML/CFT reporting entity registration evidence
Pro-forma client engagement terms for virtual CFO services
Flow-of-funds and expected transaction volume statement for payment processors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or a payment processor declines or 'de-risks' the application, engage an independent trust and company service provider (TCSP) agent in New Zealand to perform enhanced due diligence, raise an escalated review with the institution's local anti-financial crime unit, or apply to an approved alternative payment institution; unresolved service refusal may be reported to the Financial Markets Authority for financial services accessibility review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) - licensing of Financial Advice Providers under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) - AML/CFT reporting entity registration and supervision; New Zealand Companies Office - professional services registry compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Advice Provider (FAP) Licence (Part 6, Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013) and AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration (Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category D (Low Impact Professional Services): no Environmental Impact Assessment or discharge consent is required because the virtual CFO and multi-currency ledger bookkeeping operation generates no manufacturing effluent, no point-source air emissions, and no land disturbance; the activity is exclusively office-based / cloud-based and is located in a service commercial zoning category.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at the corporate layer: the company produces no regulated wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams. The principal environmental obligations are indirect and address (i) e-waste and secure data destruction under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, (ii) energy consumption of the registered office building within the tenant lease's green covenant, and (iii) cloud service provider emissions disclosed in the company's ESG appendix - none of which requires a statutory discharge permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil defence and occupational clearance is confined to the registered office premise: a current Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) and Annual Fire Safety Certificate must be maintained pursuant to the Building Act 2004 and the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017 for any leased professional office; WorkSafe New Zealand compliance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 requires a documented worker participation system, hazard register, emergency evacuation procedure, and first-aid provision for all employees operating the virtual CFO platform. No further structural load, industrial equipment, or hazardous-substance clearance is required for the virtual professional-services classification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Taake, Wellington, New Zealand. Secure online portal: myIR at ird.govt.nz. For a Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) relying on offshore tax-exempt status, the separate Cook Islands tax administration handles the exemption, but all New Zealand income tax, GST, PAYE, and withholding tax registrations and filings are administered by the New Zealand IRD.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated or non-resident entity, including an International Company (CK_IC), is not automatically registered for New Zealand tax. The entity must apply for a New Zealand IRD number if it derives New Zealand-sourced income, makes taxable supplies subject to New Zealand GST, employs workers in New Zealand, or becomes tax resident through central management and control being exercised in New Zealand. The standard procedure is: (1) confirm that the entity is not incorporated in New Zealand and therefore not automatically registered under the Companies Act 1993; (2) obtain the entity’s certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office details, director details, and proof of non-resident status; (3) submit Form IR596 or use the non-resident application pathway in myIR; (4) for GST, file a separate registration application through myIR or the GST registration form; (5) if no New Zealand address is available, appoint a New Zealand tax agent; and (6) use the resulting IRD number for all New Zealand tax obligations, including GST, PAYE, and non-resident withholding tax. A CK_IC that earns only foreign-source income and has no New Zealand compliance nexus is not required to obtain an IRD number solely by reason of being an International Company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone. The CK_IC International Company is an offshore, non-resident limited liability vehicle: it is not resident in New Zealand for income tax purposes unless its central management and control is in New Zealand. It is not a pass-through entity and not an ordinary New Zealand resident company. It is not subject to New Zealand corporate tax on non-New-Zealand-source income. A New Zealand-incorporated ordinary company carrying on the same outsourced virtual CFO activity would instead be an Entity_Level_Taxation resident company subject to 28% income tax on worldwide income. If New Zealand-resident shareholders control the CK_IC, the New Zealand controlled foreign company rules may attribute certain passive income to those shareholders despite the entity-level tax exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no US-style check-the-box election. Entity classification follows legal form, place of incorporation, and tax residence. Available elections relevant to a New Zealand tax filing entity include: (a) look-through company (LTC) election under subpart HG of the Income Tax Act 2007 for qualifying New Zealand resident companies; (b) consolidated group election for New Zealand resident companies; (c) GST grouping and joint GST registration elections under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; (d) voluntary GST registration for non-residents making or intending to make taxable supplies in New Zealand; (e) provisional tax payment frequency options; and (f) adjustment and documentation positions under the hybrid mismatch rules in Part FH of the Income Tax Act 2007. A CK_IC cannot elect out of the New Zealand CFC attribution rules through a check-the-box mechanism, and the general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 remains applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — New Zealand value added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000. Compulsory GST registration arises when a person carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand and the value of taxable supplies made in New Zealand in any 12-month period exceeds NZD 60,000. A non-resident supplier of remote or digital services supplied to New Zealand resident consumers is also required to register when total supplies to New Zealand consumers exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold if the supplier is carrying on a taxable activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not currently impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority API clearance, or digital stamping requirement for e-invoices. Electronic invoicing is accepted and the New Zealand Government participates in the Peppol network, requiring government agencies to receive e-invoices from suppliers. The IRD does not operate a pre-clearance gateway; instead, GST-registered persons must issue compliant GST invoices, maintain complete electronic or paper records, and keep those records for seven years. E-invoice content must satisfy the GST invoice requirements, and the integrity, readability, and accessibility of the electronic record must be preserved.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods supplied in New Zealand may be zero-rated if the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand, normally within 28 days of supply, and retains contemporaneous export evidence. Services may be zero-rated under section 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the recipient is a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, and the services are not supplied directly in connection with New Zealand land, not supplied directly in connection with goods situated in New Zealand, and not supplied to a person resident in New Zealand at the time of performance. For outsourced virtual CFO services, zero-rating requires evidence that the client is a non-resident, the services are received and enjoyed offshore, and the supply is not consumed in New Zealand. Cloud-based delivery, use of Stripe or Wise, and an offshore contract are supporting factors but are not dispositive if management, staff, or service performance are in New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service) for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment out of New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of offshore consideration
Signed service agreement or engagement letter identifying the non-resident client
GST-compliant tax invoice or e-invoice describing the exported services and the offshore recipient
Service delivery records, workpapers, IP logs, meeting records, and project files demonstrating offshore performance and foreign receipt of the services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The IRD may audit zero-rated export supplies to confirm physical export of goods or offshore receipt and enjoyment of services. If the supporting documentation is inadequate or the export or non-resident condition fails, the supply becomes standard-rated at 15%, the taxpayer must account for output GST, and any GST refund previously claimed is recoverable with use-of-money interest. Shortfall penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, up to 40% for an unacceptable tax position, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. False or fraudulent zero-rating claims may also lead to criminal prosecution. A tax-exempt International Company whose substantive activity is in New Zealand, or whose New Zealand resident controllers use the exemption to avoid tax, may additionally be challenged under section BG 1 and the CFC attribution rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — the sole monetary authority and operator of the NZD settlement-asset system (Exchange Settlement Account System, ESAS) under which all NZD clearing and settlement for the International Company's treasury accounts occurs; the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) serves as the registry-tier corporate regulator of the International Company (CK_IC), while the New Zealand Financial Markets Authority (FMA) supervises the financial service providers used by the IC; the NZD is the functional and reporting currency of the IC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalized, free-floating exchange-rate regime with no exchange-control legislation. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are unconditionally convertible; there are no prior-approval, licensing, quota, or repatriation-restriction mechanisms applicable to NZD or foreign-currency operations. Profit remittance, dividend distributions, intercompany loan servicing, principal repayments, and liquidation proceeds may be repatriated freely to any jurisdiction without central-bank consent, subject only to standard transaction-monitoring obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and the internal treasury policy of the correspondent bank. As a tax-exempt Cook Islands International Company (exempt under the Cook Islands International Companies Act 2011-12), the CK_IC faces no exchange-control overlay beyond the limitations, if any, contained in its own trust deed or instrument of incorporation and the NZD remains fully convertible against USD, EUR, GBP, and AUD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist. New Zealand abolished all exchange controls following the 1984 currency float, and no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation applies to export receipts, foreign-currency earnings, or invoice collections. The CK_IC may retain export-derived service fees indefinitely in USD, EUR, GBP, or any other acceptable currency in multi-currency accounts, or convert them to NZD at prevailing market rates without filing any return to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand or the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission. Expatriation of funds is equally unrestricted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — primary NZD multicurrency treasury account with USD/EUR/GBP sub-ledgers and SWIFT GPI outbound capability
Operational Account — secondary NZD/USD settlement account with dedicated corporate FX desk and same-day ESAS clearing

Capital Escrow Account — segregated client-funds trust account for advance advisory fees held under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, paired with an operational account
Operational Account — contingency NZD account with digital-first onboarding for non-resident corporates
Operational Account — domestic backup account only, limited cross-border FX capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High — Wise (formerly TransferWise) is the preferred fintech/EMI partner: it is registered as a Financial Service Provider in New Zealand (FSP number 336766) and operates as a non-bank money remitter holding funds via safeguarding arrangements with Tier-1 NZ banks, with the ability to issue a NZD local bank-account number (BBAN) and execute SWIFT MT103 outbound USD/EUR/GBP payments. Airwallex and Payoneer are viable secondary EMIs for collecting virtual-CFO subscription fees and paying international subcontractors. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs are not licensed banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989; therefore funds held with Wise/Airwallex are not 'protected deposits' under the Depositor Compensation Scheme and carry counterparty credit risk; (ii) under the AML/CFT Act 2009, the EMI must apply enhanced due diligence (EDD) to a tax-exempt offshore International Company, which typically requires the CK_IC to provide certified registry documents from the Cook Islands Financial Services Development Authority (FISDA), a source-of-funds declaration, and evidence of the beneficial-ownership chain; (iii) the Cook Islands' removal from the FATF grey list in October 2024 has materially reduced onboarding refusals, but residual reputational caution remains at tier-1 banks and legacy compliance teams; (iv) the CK_IC must maintain a Cook Islands registered agent and a New Zealand nexus (management/control in Auckland or Christchurch) to satisfy both the EMI's jurisdictional policy and the bank's substance expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the Tier-1 commercial banks (ANZ, BNZ, Westpac), fully remote account opening is generally unavailable for a tax-exempt offshore International Company. The AML/CFT Act 2009 and the banks' internal EDD frameworks require at least one director and every ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) owning 25% or more to attend an in-person interview at a New Zealand branch (Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch) or, alternatively, to execute identity and residency verification before a New Zealand-recognized notary, justice of the peace, or New Zealand embassy consular officer, with certified hard-copy originals couriered to the bank. ASB and Kiwibank typically decline fully remote onboarding of Cook Islands ICs altogether. By contrast, the digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex) permit 100% remote onboarding via live video verification of the directors and UBOs, but reserve the right to demand a certified corporate-registry bundle (Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, Incumbency Certificate) issued by FISDA and a bank reference from the existing relationship bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company status (Cook Islands IC) — perceived jurisdiction risk and historical FATF grey-listing (November 2021 – October 2024)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Cook Islands Financial Services Development Authority (FISDA); Certificate of Good Standing dated within 30 days of the application; statutory Tax Exemption Certificate confirming non-resident tax-exempt status; a formal legal opinion from Cook Islands counsel confirming the IC's valid existence, limited liability, non-resident classification, and absence of local tax liability; FATF grey-list exit communication of October 2024; and an excerpt of the International Companies Act 2011-12 showing the exempt-company regime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical substance or economic activity in the Cook Islands (economic-substance red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The IC maintains its registered office at a licensed Cook Islands registered agent's premises; the outsourced virtual CFO management and multicurrency bookkeeping services are actually executed in New Zealand under a Management Services Agreement (MSA); provide the executed MSA, the NZ premises lease or virtual-office correspondence of the NZ service provider, employee or contractor agreements with NZ-based accountants, and signed client service contracts evidencing genuine commercial activity; a board resolution confirming that management and control are exercised in New Zealand, which is treated by NZ banks as acceptable substance within the Realm of New Zealand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership chain (trust structure or corporate shareholder)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete UBO chart extending to every natural person controlling 25% or more of the IC; certified passport copies and dated utility bills or bank statements for each UBO; the underlying trust deed or declaration of trust (redacted to protect beneficiary privacy but sufficient to trace legal and beneficial ownership); a Certificate of Incumbency from the Cook Islands registered agent; and a written source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement covering the initial capital injection, signed by the settlor or contributing shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multicurrency client-funds handling and inbound remittances triggering money-laundering suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written Client-Funds Handling Policy evidencing strict segregation of the IC's operational funds from client funds; a statutory trust-account ledger (escrow account) compliant with the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; a Xero or equivalent general-ledger extract reconciling each inbound payment to an executed advisory agreement; client onboarding files including beneficial-ownership disclosures and AML warranties; and a written declaration that the IC never accepts third-party consolidated payments or unexplained intercompany pass-through wires.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The subscribing shareholder (e.g., a Hong Kong or Singapore holding company) effects the capital injection as a SWIFT MT103 wire to the CK_IC's NZD operational account at ANZ Bank New Zealand or BNZ. The payment narrative must read 'Equity contribution — share subscription' (no mandatory purpose code is prescribed by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, but the bank's internal form requires a standard reason-for-payment selection). For USD or EUR injections, the receiving bank applies a same-day spot conversion into NZD at the prevailing interbank rate plus a 2–3 pip margin after deduction of SWIFT correspondents' charges; treasury policy should instruct 'OUR' for all inward charges. No Overseas Investment Office (OIO) approval is required because the IC does not acquire 'sensitive land' or 'significant business assets' within the meaning of the Overseas Investment Act 2005, s. 12. The complete verification bundle comprises: a notarized board resolution approving the allotment, the share allotment register updated with FISDA, the Certificate of Incumbency, a bank reference from the sending bank, and a source-of-funds declaration; the bank may additionally require the trust deed if the shareholder is a trust vehicle.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements (subcontractor fees, software subscriptions, bank charges, and lease payments) clear through: (i) the Payments NZ High-Value Clearing System (HVCS) and Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) for domestic NZD payments; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border USD/EUR/GBP supplier and contractor payments, preferably via SWIFT GPI for real-time tracking; and (iii) Wise Business multi-currency rails with local-nostro conversion for low-value recurring technology subscriptions (Xero, QuickBooks, Stripe, and Notion). Dividend distributions to the shareholder execute via SWIFT MT103 with narrative 'Dividend distribution — IC Act 2011-12', supported by a signed solvency certificate and a board distribution resolution; no withholding tax applies because the CK_IC is tax-exempt and non-resident in the Cook Islands, and New Zealand source taxation does not arise on distributions made by a foreign IC to foreign shareholders. Commercial letters of credit are not commercially standard for virtual CFO services; where a client requires bank-assurance, a standby letter of credit (SBLC) or documentary collection (documents against payment) is available from ANZ or Westpac at issuance fees of 50–150 basis points per annum, but the IC should discourage LC usage in its standard terms. Treasury policy requires a minimum one-month NZD liquidity buffer of not less than NZD 50,000 in the operational account to cover payroll, statutory filing, and clearing obligations, and prohibits same-day disbursement of received funds pending 24-hour KYC-funds verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward contracts in NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, and NZD/GBP for maturities of 1–12 months, executed under a 2018 ISDA FX Definitions master agreement or the New Zealand Financial Markets Association (NZFMA) standard terms; quoted at 20–30 basis points annualized for major NZD pairs; no Reserve Bank approval required.
FX swaps and roll-over (tom-next, spot-forward, and forward-forward) for temporary liquidity conversion between NZD and USD/EUR without triggering a realized gain or loss for treasury reporting.

Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) for structural hedging of a multicurrency intercompany loan or shareholder advance, including principal and interest exposure, with settlement through the Tier-1 bank's derivatives desk.

European-style vanilla FX options (calls, puts, straddles, and zero-cost collars) on NZD/USD and NZD/EUR, available once the IC executes an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex (CSA) and posts the required margin.
Natural hedging through multi-currency account pooling and notional cash-pooling (available at Westpac and ANZ), converting only the net residual multicurrency position at the monthly treasury close.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on NZD are legally permissible but commercially inadvisable and not used in New Zealand because the NZD is fully convertible and deliverable; the deliverable forward market offers materially tighter spreads and eliminates settlement risk; any proposal to execute an NDF should be rejected by the IC's treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies – New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the annual return date, which is normally the anniversary of incorporation; the Registrar issues a reminder notice to the registered office at least one month before the due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The company is placed in default; the Registrar may initiate administrative strike-off under Section 318 of the Companies Act 1993 if the annual return remains unfiled after a notice of intention to remove; directors also face a maximum monetary penalty of NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000) per offence for failure to deliver required information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Auditor’s Report (mandatory public filing only if the company is 'large' or has 25 or more shareholders)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (public register) and, where applicable, the Financial Markets Authority (FMA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be delivered to the Companies Office within 20 working days after the balance date for FMC reporting entities and for companies required to file under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; for exempt private companies that voluntarily opt in, the filing deadline aligns with the annual return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited financial statements is an offence under Sections 203-204 of the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013; directors are liable to a maximum fine of NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000) per offence, and the Registrar may refuse the annual return and initiate administrative strike-off; the FMA may impose additional civil penalties for reporting failures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office / Registered Agent Retainer Confirmation and Change Notices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No direct filing if no changes occur; any change is lodged with the New Zealand Companies Office on Companies Act forms
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The company must maintain a registered office in New Zealand at all times; changes of registered office are notified to the Registrar within 10 working days of the change; agent retainer is renewed annually on the incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the company ceases to have a registered office in New Zealand, the Registrar may remove the company from the register after due notice; directors who fail to notify a change of registered office commit an offence under Section 202 of the Companies Act 1993 and are liable to a fine of up to NZD 10,000 (approx. USD 6,000) per contravention.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory under Sections 200 and 207 of the Companies Act 1993 (NZ) if: (a) the company has 25 or more shareholders at any time during the accounting period; (b) the company is 'large' — total assets exceed NZD 60 million (approx. USD 36 million) or total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million (approx. USD 18 million) at the balance date or in each of the two preceding accounting periods; (c) the company is a registered FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; or (d) shareholders holding 5% or more of the votes deliver a valid audit requisition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand statutory financial statements must be prepared in accordance with XRB accounting standards: NZ IFRS (Tier 1) for large FMC reporting entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR, Tier 2) for smaller reporting entities; New Zealand GAAP (Tier 3) for moderate-size non-reporting companies; and the simplified Tier 4 framework (FRS for small- and micro-entities). An exempt private International Company providing outsourced CFO services may adopt NZ IFRS RDR unless it qualifies for the simplified Tier 4 format; all statements must present a true and fair view and comply with the Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a standalone annual UBO declaration for private companies; the annual return to the Companies Office serves as the statutory annual confirmation of current members and directors. For an International Company (Tax Exempt Zone) the company must maintain an up-to-date Register of Members at the registered office; share allotments are filed with the Companies Office on Form 35 (Return of Allotment) within 10 working days of the event; director changes are filed on Form 17 (Notice of Change of Directors) within 10 working days. Share transfers that do not involve a new allotment are recorded only in the internal Register of Members and are confirmed to the Registrar in the next annual return. The Registrar may at any time issue a verification notice demanding production of the on-site registers; defective registers constitute an offence subject to fines under the Companies Act 1993.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% flat income tax rate for companies under Schedule 1, Part A of the Income Tax Act 2007; no provincial or local tax surcharge.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays or preferential zones in New Zealand. Incentives include a 15% R&D tax credit, the imputation credit system for resident shareholders, and the exemption of foreign-source income for non-resident companies that are not tax resident under an applicable double tax agreement (DTA). For an International Company that lacks a New Zealand permanent establishment and derives virtual CFO fees from non-residents, the effective rate is nil on foreign-source income; however, services physically performed in New Zealand are treated as New Zealand-source income and will be taxed at 28%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No finite carry-forward limit. Losses may be carried forward indefinitely under section IA 5 of the Income Tax Act 2007, subject to 49% shareholder continuity; a stricter continuity requirement applies to CFC losses.
